title: GCSE (1 – 9) Bounds
instructions: Use black ink or ball-point pen.
Answer the questions in the spaces provided – there may be more space than you need.
Diagrams are NOT accurately drawn, unless otherwise indicated.
You must show all your working out.
information: The marks for each question are shown in brackets – use this as a guide as to how much time to spend on each question.
advice: Read each question carefully before you start to answer it.
Keep an eye on the time.
Check your answers if you have time at the end

parts.text: A rectangle has a length of 21cm, to the nearest cm, and a width of 5.3cm, to the nearest mm. Work out the upper bound for the perimeter of the rectangle.
parts.explanation:
21 cm to the nearest cm gives 20.5 ≤ length < 21.5.
5.3 cm to the nearest mm gives 5.25 ≤ width < 5.35.
The perimeter is largest when both sides are largest:
UB = 2 × (21.5 + 5.35) = 2 × 26.85 = 53.7 cm

parts.text: Work out the lower bound for the area of the rectangle.
parts.explanation:
The area is smallest when both sides are smallest:
LB = 20.5 × 5.25 = 107.625 cm²

parts.text: A circle has a radius of 5cm, to the nearest cm. Work out the lower bound for the circumference of the circle. Give your answer in terms of π.
parts.explanation:
5 cm to the nearest cm gives 4.5 ≤ radius < 5.5.
The circumference is smallest when the radius is smallest:
LB = 2 × π × 4.5 = 9π cm

parts.text: Work out the upper bound for the area of the circle. Give your answer in terms of π.
parts.explanation:
The area is largest when the radius is largest:
UB = π × 5.5² = 30.25π cm²

parts.text: A rectangular field has a length of 105 metres, to the nearest 5 metres, and a width of 53 metres, to the nearest metre. Work out the lower bound for the perimeter of the field.
parts.explanation:
105 m to the nearest 5 m gives 102.5 ≤ length < 107.5.
53 m to the nearest m gives 52.5 ≤ width < 53.5.
The perimeter is smallest when both sides are smallest:
LB = 2 × (102.5 + 52.5) = 2 × 155 = 310 m

parts.text: Work out the upper bound for the area of the field.
parts.explanation:
The area is largest when both sides are largest:
UB = 107.5 × 53.5 = 5751.25 m²

parts.text: A circle has a radius of 5.36cm, correct to 2 decimal places. Work out the lower bound for the circumference of the circle. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
parts.explanation:
5.36 cm to 2 decimal places gives 5.355 ≤ radius < 5.365.
The circumference is smallest when the radius is smallest:
LB = 2 × π × 5.355 = 33.6464... = 33.65 cm (2 d.p.)

parts.text: Work out the upper bound for the area of the circle. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
parts.explanation:
The area is largest when the radius is largest:
UB = π × 5.365² = π × 28.783225 = 90.4251... = 90.4 cm² (3 s.f.)

questions.text: s = 4.15 correct to 2 decimal places, t = 2.516 correct to 3 decimal places, v = s/t. Work out the upper bound for v. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.
questions.explanation:
s = 4.15 (2 d.p.) gives 4.145 ≤ s < 4.155.
t = 2.516 (3 d.p.) gives 2.5155 ≤ t < 2.5165.
A quotient is largest with the largest numerator and the smallest denominator:
UB = 4.155 ÷ 2.5155 = 1.65175... = 1.652 (3 d.p.)

questions.text: I = 5.92 correct to 2 decimal places, R = 12.356 correct to 3 decimal places, V = IR. Work out the upper bound for V. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.
questions.explanation:
I = 5.92 (2 d.p.) gives 5.915 ≤ I < 5.925.
R = 12.356 (3 d.p.) gives 12.3555 ≤ R < 12.3565.
A product is largest when both factors are largest:
UB = 5.925 × 12.3565 = 73.2122625 = 73.212 (3 d.p.)

questions.text: a = 5.3 cm correct to the nearest mm, b = 8.2 cm correct to the nearest mm. Calculate the lower bound for c. You must show all your working. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.explanation:
a = 5.3 cm to the nearest mm gives 5.25 ≤ a < 5.35.
b = 8.2 cm to the nearest mm gives 8.15 ≤ b < 8.25.
By Pythagoras, c = √(a² + b²), which is smallest when a and b are smallest:
LB = √(5.25² + 8.15²) = √(27.5625 + 66.4225) = √93.985 = 9.6945... = 9.69 cm (3 s.f.)

questions.text: a = 4.1 cm correct to the nearest mm, c = 10 cm correct to the nearest cm. Calculate the lower bound for b. You must show all your working. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation:
a = 4.1 cm to the nearest mm gives 4.05 ≤ a < 4.15.
c = 10 cm to the nearest cm gives 9.5 ≤ c < 10.5.
By Pythagoras, b = √(c² − a²), which is smallest when c is smallest and a is largest:
LB = √(9.5² − 4.15²) = √(90.25 − 17.2225) = √73.0275 = 8.5456... = 8.5 cm (1 d.p.)

questions.text: E = 812 correct to 3 significant figures, T = 9.2 correct to 1 decimal place, P = E/T. By considering bounds, work out the value of P to a suitable degree of accuracy. Give a reason for your answer.
questions.explanation:
E = 812 (3 s.f.) gives 811.5 ≤ E < 812.5.
T = 9.2 (1 d.p.) gives 9.15 ≤ T < 9.25.
LB of P = 811.5 ÷ 9.25 = 87.7297...
UB of P = 812.5 ÷ 9.15 = 88.7978...
The bounds disagree at 2 s.f. (88 and 89) but both round to 90 to 1 s.f., so P = 90 to 1 significant figure.

questions.text: g = 12.7 correct to 3 significant figures, h = 9.294 correct to 3 decimal places, f = g/h. By considering bounds, work out the value of f to a suitable degree of accuracy. Give a reason for your answer.
questions.explanation:
g = 12.7 (3 s.f.) gives 12.65 ≤ g < 12.75.
h = 9.294 (3 d.p.) gives 9.2935 ≤ h < 9.2945.
LB of f = 12.65 ÷ 9.2945 = 1.36101...
UB of f = 12.75 ÷ 9.2935 = 1.37192...
The bounds disagree at 3 s.f. (1.36 and 1.37) but both round to 1.4 to 2 s.f., so f = 1.4 to 2 significant figures.

questions.text: F = 25.14 N correct to 2 decimal places, A = 4.29 m² correct to 3 significant figures. p = F/A. By considering bounds, work out the value of p to a suitable degree of accuracy. Give a reason for your answer.
questions.explanation:
F = 25.14 N (2 d.p.) gives 25.135 ≤ F < 25.145.
A = 4.29 m² (3 s.f.) gives 4.285 ≤ A < 4.295.
LB of p = 25.135 ÷ 4.295 = 5.85215...
UB of p = 25.145 ÷ 4.285 = 5.86814...
The bounds disagree at 3 s.f. (5.85 and 5.87) but both round to 5.9 to 2 s.f., so p = 5.9 Nm⁻² to 2 significant figures.

questions.text: F = 20.81 N correct to 2 decimal places, P = 5.12 Nm⁻² correct to 3 significant figures. A = F/P. By considering bounds, work out the value of A to a suitable degree of accuracy. Give a reason for your answer.
questions.explanation:
F = 20.81 N (2 d.p.) gives 20.805 ≤ F < 20.815.
P = 5.12 Nm⁻² (3 s.f.) gives 5.115 ≤ P < 5.125.
LB of A = 20.805 ÷ 5.125 = 4.05951...
UB of A = 20.815 ÷ 5.115 = 4.06940...
The bounds disagree at 3 s.f. (4.06 and 4.07) but both round to 4.1 to 2 s.f., so A = 4.1 m² to 2 significant figures.

questions.text: v = 35.2 correct to 1 decimal place, a = 9.8 correct to 1 decimal place, s = 60.35 correct to 2 decimal places, v² = u² + 2as. Work out the upper bound for u. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
